reply_text:
I fetched the page and found the words. The candidate is the same claim as one already recorded, so my reading is **recorded**.

**Page check.** The page is Legg's own blog post on vetta.org, "Goodbye 2011, hello 2012". The quote is in his reply, as "Shane Legg", to a reader called "sp". It matches the candidate word for word apart from spacing. His reply starts "Many things, but in three areas:" and point 1 reads: "The simplest and least interesting is computer performance. Seeing the same again over the next 8 years probably isn't necessary, but it will clearly make it more likely that an impressive proto-AGI will be developed." This is his own words, not a news report.

**Date.** The page as fetched shows no date for the post or for any comment. The only date is in the address, `/2011/12/`. I could not confirm the candidate's date of 2012-01-08 from the page. The reply came after the post, so it is late December 2011 or later.

**Admission.**
- **This is a repeat, not a new claim.** The forecast itself is in the post: "I expect to see an impressive proto-AGI within the next 8 years," followed by a definition and an "acid test" in an earlier reply. That is already the file `2011-12-31-legg-proto-agi-within-eight-years.toml`. The reply quotes that line back, and Legg's answer adds nothing new: the same thing, the same 8 years and so the same due year. Under the restatement rules it is one claim. At most, its date could be added to `repeated_on` once someone confirms it.
- **On its own, the sentence is weak.** Read alone, "more computing power will make a proto-AGI more likely" says what will cause a result, not what will happen. The forecast in it is borrowed from the post.
- **The speaker's role should be checked by the person reviewing this.** In 2011–12 the role history gives Legg only "co-founder of DeepMind (2010)". The rule counts a "chief executive, founder-leader or chair" or the "named chief scientist speaking for it". Whether a co-founder of DeepMind at that stage counts, and whether DeepMind then built frontier models, is a borderline question. It would apply to the existing record as well as to this candidate.
